✶Self-sabotage stems from deeply ingrained subconscious beliefs about your worth and your body — these require compassionate awareness, not more willpower.
✶Common emotional triggers (stress, boredom, loneliness, exhaustion, and reward-seeking) drive eating behaviors that have nothing to do with physical hunger.
✶Progress is infinitely more powerful than perfection — celebrating every good choice and viewing setbacks with curiosity rather than shame builds transformation that actually lasts.

Body Burn Basics

Your Quick Reference Guide

Use this quick reference guide to review the core principles of metabolic health when setting your daily goals and building your routine.

Dietary Non-Negotiables

  • Lower Insulin: It is the master switch. You are physically incapable of burning fat when insulin is high.
  • The "Fiber First" Rule: Eat fiber and protein before carbohydrates to physically blunt blood sugar and insulin spikes.
  • Prioritize Protein & Ancestral Fats: Make protein the foundation to preserve muscle and naturally stimulate GLP-1. Fuel with stable fats (butter, tallow, olive oil).
  • Avoid the Traffic Jam (Randle Cycle): Never combine heavy, refined carbohydrates with heavy fats in the exact same meal.
  • Eliminate Seed Oils & Fructose: Industrial seed oils drive fat-cell hypertrophy (sick, inflamed storage). Liquid fructose goes straight to the liver, driving severe insulin resistance.
  • TRE vs. The Rule of 3s: Healthy bodies thrive on Time-Restricted Eating (14-16 hours fasting). Stressed, chronically ill, or historically restricted bodies need exactly 3 balanced meals a day with zero snacking to signal absolute safety.
  • Don't Fear Salt: When lowering insulin, your kidneys flush sodium. Liberally salt your food to prevent fatigue and stop the hormonal stress response that actually grows fat cells.

Lifestyle & Movement

  • Build the Engine (Lift Weights): Muscle acts as a "glucose sink" and requires massive daily energy to maintain. Resistance training is non-negotiable for long-term fat loss.
  • Post-Meal "Squat Snacks": Do 15 bodyweight squats or take a 10-15 minute walk immediately after eating to force your large leg muscles to rapidly soak up glucose directly from the bloodstream.
  • Anchor Your Circadian Rhythm: Get natural sunlight in your eyes within 30 minutes of waking to regulate cortisol and set your sleep-wake hormones.
  • Protect Melatonin: Dim artificial lights at night, and finish eating 2-3 hours before bed. Eating carbs late at night spikes blood sugar precisely when rising melatonin is trying to shut the pancreas down.
  • Active Stress Management: You cannot out-diet a nervous system that thinks it's dying. Take 3 deep breaths before meals and chew thoroughly to shift into a parasympathetic (rest-and-digest) state.
  • Cold Exposure: Finish showers with 30-60 seconds of cold water to activate "brown fat," a specialized tissue packed with mitochondria that burns energy to generate heat.

Hidden Hindrances

  • Ceramides: Toxic lipid roadblocks inside your cells that make them "deaf" to insulin. They are created from fats, but the production is driven by systemic inflammation and toxins.
  • Chronic Sleep Deprivation: Just one night of poor sleep crashes leptin (satiety), spikes ghrelin (hunger), and elevates cortisol, priming the body to store fat.
  • Environmental Toxins (Obesogens): Chemicals in plastic bottles (BPA), synthetic fragrances, and pesticides mimic estrogen and disrupt natural thyroid and hormone signaling.
  • A History of Chronic Dieting: Years of starvation diets cause cellular energy failure. The body intentionally downregulates thyroid output and metabolism. You must nourish the body to prove the "famine" is over before fat loss can occur.

What to Measure & Monitor

  • Fasting Insulin: Ask your practitioner to test this, not just your A1C. A healthy, optimal fasting insulin level should ideally be below 3 to 5 uIU/mL.
  • Triglyceride-to-HDL Ratio: Look at this specific ratio rather than just total LDL cholesterol. It is a much more accurate predictor of metabolic health and cardiovascular risk.
  • Check for Deficiencies: Ensure adequate levels of Magnesium, Vitamin D, Iodine, Zinc, and Selenium (essential for thyroid hormone conversion and ATP production).
  • Thyroid Conversion: Have your practitioner check your free T3 and T4 levels to ensure your body is actively converting inactive thyroid hormone into its active form.
  • Medication Interference: Discuss your current prescriptions with your doctor, as some medications (beta-blockers, corticosteroids, antidepressants) can actively slow your resting metabolic rate or promote insulin resistance.

When to Dig Deeper: Seeking a Practitioner

If you are consistently applying these metabolic basics but your progress remains completely stalled, do not restrict your diet further. You may have underlying interferences that require a professional eye to unravel. It is time to seek out a functional medicine practitioner or qualified health professional if you suspect or experience:

  • ▪ Severe Digestive Issues: Chronic bloating, signs of a "leaky gut," or intense, immediate immune reactions to specific plant compounds (oxalates, histamines, lectins) that point to deep gut barrier dysregulation.
  • ▪ Hormone Problems: Severe menopausal symptoms, PCOS, disrupted menstrual cycles, or persistent thyroid dysfunction (especially poor T4 to T3 conversion).
  • ▪ Significant Fatigue: Waking up exhausted despite adequate sleep, heavy reliance on caffeine, or a constant "wired but tired" feeling indicating nervous system burnout or cellular energy failure.
  • ▪ Autoimmune & Inflammatory Conditions: Unexplained joint pain, persistent skin conditions (psoriasis, eczema), Hashimoto's, or any state where your immune system is locked in a hyper-reactive stress response.

Finding Your Food: A Guide to the Diets That Actually Heal

By Jaime Jenkins, Naturopathic Practitioner | Functional Nutritionist | Brain MD Coach

Dietary Frameworks

You've tried eating clean. You've googled your symptoms. You've done the research — and somehow you're more confused than when you started.

That's not your fault. That's the internet.

Every day you're hit with a new headline: Keto cured my autoimmune disease. Carnivore fixed my gut. Plant-based reversed my cancer. All of them have testimonials. All of them contradict each other. And none of them explain why they work — which means you have no idea which one is right for you.

This section fixes that.

Here's what almost no one tells you: the reason these diets all show results has almost nothing to do with what makes them different from each other. It's what they all have in common — they cut out highly processed, artificial foods and return you to whole, single-ingredient nutrition. If you've been eating the Standard American Diet, that one shift alone will change everything.

But if you're dealing with something deeper — thyroid dysfunction, chronic gut distress, autoimmune flare-ups, or a body that just won't respond — a general clean diet won't be enough. You need a foundation. And that foundation is the elimination diet.

Once that's in place, every other framework you've heard about starts to make sense. Not as a trend to follow — but as a tool with a specific job.

Read this section once and you'll never need to "research diets" again.

Where to Start

If healthy eating feels completely foreign to you — if you've never really cooked your own food or paid attention to what you put in your body — I want you to hear this: you don't need to overhaul everything overnight.

Start with one move: cut out the processed, packaged stuff and replace it with real, single-ingredient food. That's it. Call it Paleo if you want a label. Call it Mediterranean. Call it "I just stopped eating things that come in a box." The name doesn't matter — the principle does.

Then stack just 1 to 3 small habits from this guide on top of that foundation. Cut out snacking between meals. Take a short walk or do a few squats right after you eat. These aren't tricks — they're metabolic levers, and they work fast. Most people are genuinely shocked by how quickly their body responds when they stop fighting it.

Once that foundation feels solid, then you start dialing in. That's when the specific dietary frameworks below become useful — not as rules to follow blindly, but as tools designed for specific biological problems.

Here's how the most popular ones actually work, and when to use each.

There is no single "perfect diet" for every human body.

What there is — is the right diet for your body, at this stage of your healing. The difference between a diet that transforms your health and one that leaves you frustrated, inflamed, and blaming yourself for failing? It is not willpower. It is not discipline. It is not even the specific foods on the list.

It is context.

The following five dietary frameworks are the ones I return to most often in my practice — each one designed for a specific metabolic situation, a specific level of gut health, a specific set of symptoms. Read through all of them. Notice which one feels like it is describing you.

The Paleo Diet

The Goal: Ancestral eating to lower systemic inflammation and remove modern agricultural triggers.

How it Works: The Paleo framework operates on the evolutionary biology premise that human genetics have not fully adapted to the foods introduced during the agricultural revolution. It focuses exclusively on foods our hunter-gatherer ancestors had access to: high-quality meat, fish, eggs, vegetables, fruits, nuts, and seeds. It strictly eliminates modern grains (especially hybridized wheat), conventional dairy, legumes, industrial seed oils, and refined sugars.

Metabolic Benefit: Because it naturally removes the most common dietary allergens (gluten and dairy) and entirely eliminates hyper-processed foods, the Paleo diet is incredibly effective for cooling systemic inflammation and healing a "leaky gut." By removing refined carbohydrates, it naturally lowers the daily insulin burden.

Best For: Individuals transitioning away from a standard American diet who want a sustainable, long-term lifestyle. It is excellent for those with general inflammation, mild to moderate insulin resistance, or those looking to naturally manage autoimmune symptoms without needing to track every single carbohydrate.

The Mediterranean Diet

The Goal: Heart health, cellular longevity, and antioxidant support.

How it Works: The true Mediterranean diet—not the Americanized version heavily reliant on massive plates of pasta—is built around an abundance of monounsaturated fats (like high-quality, cold-pressed olive oil), fatty fish (like sardines and wild salmon), fresh vegetables, herbs, and moderate amounts of nuts and seeds, while limiting red meat and highly processed foods.

Metabolic Benefit: The metabolic power of this diet comes from its immense concentration of Omega-3 fatty acids and oleic acid. These specific fats are required by your mitochondria to build healthy, fluid cell membranes, allowing your cells to communicate and produce energy efficiently. It is also packed with polyphenols (antioxidants) from fresh herbs and olive oil, which actively neutralize the oxidative stress and free radicals that damage metabolism.

Best For \& How to Tweak It: Excellent for general longevity, cardiovascular health, and brain health. However, if your primary goal is weight loss and reversing severe insulin resistance, you must modify the traditional Mediterranean approach by keeping the "whole grains" and fruit portions very minimal so that you do not continue to spike your blood sugar.

Ketogenic (Keto) / Low-Carb

The Goal: Forcing metabolic flexibility and rapid fat adaptation.

How it Works: Restricts carbohydrates to a very low level (usually under 30-50g a day), forcing the liver to burn stored fat and produce ketones for energy.

When to Avoid \& What to Do Instead: However, for those who have very dysregulated nervous systems, are highly stressed, chronically tired and sick, have POTS, or those who have chronically restricted themselves and have significant weight loss resistance, this approach may be too stressful on their system. If their mitochondria are operating on low, they need to rebuild their cellular energy first before they can ever adapt well to fat metabolism in the keto or carnivore diet. Instead, these individuals need active nervous system regulation and a more moderate dietary approach. While they still need to monitor carbohydrate intake to prevent insulin spikes, they will do much better eating a consistent three meals a day to provide steady, safe energy signals to the body.

The Carnivore Diet

The Goal: The ultimate elimination protocol for deep gut healing and severe autoimmune management.

How it Works: Consists entirely of animal products: ruminant meats (beef, lamb), fish, eggs, bone broth, and animal fats (tallow, butter, ghee). It completely eliminates all plant foods, including vegetables, fruits, grains, nuts, and seeds.

Metabolic Benefit: While plants contain many beneficial nutrients, they also contain natural defense chemicals (like oxalates, lectins, and phytates). For a healthy person, these are harmless. But for someone with a severely damaged or hyper-permeable gut lining, these plant compounds can act as sandpaper, triggering constant, crippling immune responses. Carnivore removes 100% of these potential plant toxins and fiber, giving the digestive tract absolute rest. Because it is functionally a "zero-carb" diet, it keeps insulin incredibly low, forces deep ketosis, and provides the body with the most highly bioavailable forms of protein, zinc, iron, and B-vitamins to rebuild depleted cellular machinery.

Best For: This is a powerful therapeutic tool for individuals suffering from severe autoimmune conditions (like Rheumatoid Arthritis or severe psoriasis), crippling digestive disorders (like severe IBS or SIBO), profound mood and psychiatric disorders, or extreme insulin resistance that hasn't responded to standard low-carb diets. It is often used as a short-to-medium-term reset before slowly reintroducing safe plant foods.

The Truth About Food Sensitivities

Lectins, Oxalates, and Histamines — Why These Diets Help (And What They're Really Fixing)

You have likely heard of popular diets centered around eliminating specific plant compounds like lectins, oxalates, or histamines. While it is entirely true that we can be highly reactive to these compounds — and eliminating them can bring profound, immediate relief — it is critical to understand why these diets feel so helpful. The plants themselves are rarely the root enemy. The relief you feel centers on three fundamental issues:

  • 1. Sheer Quantity and Evolutionary Mismatch

    Defense chemicals like oxalates and lectins are naturally found in high amounts in foods like grains and legumes. Our ancient ancestors did not have constant, year-round access to these foods, nor did they consume them in massive quantities. Today, we eat substantially more of these compounds than our evolutionary biology can comprehend. The sheer volume simply overloads the system.

  • 2. An Overactive Immune System

    We are living in an environment that keeps our immune system in a constant state of hyper-reactivity. Being stuck in a chronic stress response, exposure to modern environmental toxins, and improper baseline nutrition all keep the immune system on high alert, causing it to aggressively attack compounds it might otherwise tolerate.

  • 3. Gut Dysregulation (The Broken Barrier)

    This is the ultimate root cause. Between 70% and 80% of your entire immune system resides in your gut. When your gut is damaged, it sends chaotic, improper messages to those immune cells. Furthermore, a broken gut barrier fails to properly digest food — instead of keeping molecules safely inside the digestive tract until they are fully broken down, a "leaky" gut allows large, undigested food particles and toxins to slip directly into your bloodstream, triggering a massive inflammatory attack.

When you eliminate lectins or oxalates, you feel better because you stop poking a gaping wound. But to truly heal, you must repair the gut lining and regulate the immune system so your body can once again tolerate the world around it. That is exactly what the Elimination Diet below is designed to do.

The Elimination Diet

The Foundation Beneath Every Other Diet

The Core Idea: If you are struggling with unresolved health issues, this is where you start — before anything else. Not because it is the most restrictive, but because it is the most revealing. It is the diagnostic tool that tells you exactly which foods are keeping your body in a state of war with itself.

How It Works: We temporarily remove the most common inflammatory triggers — gluten, dairy, soy, eggs, corn, and nightshades — not as a permanent restriction, but as a reset. When the body is no longer fighting a constant stream of triggers, inflammation cools, symptoms often dramatically improve, and we gain a clear baseline. Then we carefully reintroduce foods one at a time to identify your specific culprits.

The good news: many foods that trigger you today may be tolerated again after your body has had the chance to heal.

You May Need an Elimination Diet If You Are Experiencing:
  • Mental Health Issues — Severe anxiety, depression, mood swings, or brain fog (often directly linked to neuroinflammation originating in the gut)
  • Chronic Inflammation — Persistent joint pain, stiffness, or skin conditions like eczema, acne, or psoriasis
  • Significant Fatigue — Waking exhausted, heavy reliance on caffeine, or severe afternoon energy crashes despite adequate sleep
  • Autoimmune Conditions — Hashimoto's thyroiditis, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Celiac disease, or any condition where the immune system is attacking the body
The most important thing I want you to hear:

You are not broken. Your body is not failing you randomly. There are real, tangible, findable reasons why you feel the way you do — and most of them can be addressed from your own home, with the right roadmap.

I know because I lived it.

    For Those Who Are Done Settling for "Manage It" — and Ready to Actually Heal

    I spent decades being told what I had — but never why I had it, and never how to get rid of it.

    I sat in sterile offices with clipboard-wielding doctors who gave my suffering a name and sent me home. Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. Chronic pain. Brain fog. I was handed diagnoses like consolation prizes — here, at least now you know what to call it — but nothing changed.

    So I went looking myself.

    I have tried it all. I mean that literally. I spent tens of thousands of dollars — on naturopaths, on specialized detox practitioners, on experimental IV therapies, on protocols that sounded promising and protocols that sounded absolutely unhinged. I ran the gamut. The cleanses. The chelation. The ozone. The cutting-edge, the time-tested, and the deeply questionable. If it existed, I probably tried it.

    And here is what that bought me — something no textbook could have given me: I now know exactly what helps, what is worth the cost, and what is an expensive waste of your time and hope. I learned it the hard way so you do not have to.

    What I eventually discovered — through years of relentless searching, through study under the world's leading functional medicine doctors, through my own body's long and difficult journey back to health — is that the body does not break down randomly. There are reasons. There are root causes. And when you find them and address them properly, the body has a profound, almost miraculous capacity to heal.

    That is what I want to help you do.

    The Deep Healing Intensive is my most personal, most comprehensive offering — and I only take a handful of clients at a time. This is not a program. It is not a course. It is not a generic protocol handed to you in a PDF. It is me — fully present, fully invested — in your healing.
